quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless another vehicle is ahead), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Move around your lane position to see better, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: The clothing you wear while riding should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and the motorcycle itself. Good clothing also protects you if you crash.

questions.question: If riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, you should travel in a:
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles should use a staggered formation. Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this, so groups should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, plus other injuries.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids as a result of braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the brake smoothly.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: Texas law requires motorcycles be equipped with certain equipment. Which of the following is not a required piece of equipment?
questions.explanation: Texas law requires horns, mirrors, steering systems, brakes, tires, wheels, exhaust systems, tail lamps, stop lamps, license plate lamps, rear reflectors, and headlamps. Your motorcycle must also have the proper identification number.

questions.question: When riding in a lane of traffic, a motorcycle operator:

options.text: Should always ride in the same part of the lane.
Should vary their lane position according to riding conditions.
Should always ride in the center of the lane.
Should always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should vary their lane position according to riding conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Move around your lane based on road and traffic conditions to stay safe.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hand ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: You should maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. When conditions are not ideal, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: How do you brake hard in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together at the same time without locking either wheel. This gives you the best braking power in a straight line.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Do whatever you can, including swerving into other lanes, to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane. Swerving to avoid a small animal can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than causing a crash with another car.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?

options.text: Move your shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down. Release the throttle and use your brakes if needed.

questions.question: In Texas, who must wear a helmet?

options.text: All motorcycle and moped operators and passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: All motorcycle and moped operators and passengers.
questions.explanation: In Texas, all motorcycle and moped operators and passengers must wear helmets while riding. Some exemptions may apply.

questions.question: When should motorcycle riders wear hearing protection?

options.text: At all times to prevent hearing damage.
Never, because it muffles important sounds like horns and sirens.
Never, because helmets provide enough protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a helmet. Earplugs and hearing protection allow you to hear important sounds like horns and sirens while protecting your hearing.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve to the side with fewer hazards.

questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control. However, on a surface with good traction, you can keep the rear brake locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: On a good surface, you can keep the rear brake locked until you stop. You should still be able to steer your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause your motorcycle to wobble?
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not accelerate to try to stop a wobble.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride when entering a highway or curve?

options.text: In the far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is usually better otherwise.
